Subject: CacheVelocity — partner onboarding: subprocessor roster + EU routing

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the intro and for taking a look at CacheVelocity as a candidate CDN/cache partner for Redwood EU customers. Were excited to get started. For compliance gating we usually share a short package up front so you can validate theres no egress or unapproved subprocessors for EU-only workloads.

Quick summary:
- Purpose: edge caching + regional traffic routing for inference artifacts (no model training).
- Scope: cache nodes in EU regions, log collection for operational metrics, optional upload acceleration.

Ive attached our current subprocessor roster (CacheVelocity_subprocessors_2028-09.xlsx) and a high-level dataflow diagram (CacheVelocity_svc_dataflow_v1.pdf). Key points:
- We operate dedicated caching clusters in eu-west-1 / eu-central-1.
- Persistent logs are retained in EU for EU customers by default.
- We use a third-party log shipper (LogSight) for aggregated metrics — LogSight is headquartered in the US but we have an EU tenancy option; details in the spreadsheet.

Can you confirm what your compliance team needs from us to clear the roster? Typical asks we see: SOC2, dataflow diagram, confirmation on KMS/location of keys, and any DPA addendum text.

Attachments: CacheVelocity_subprocessors_2028-09.xlsx, CacheVelocity_svc_dataflow_v1.pdf

Thanks,

Appreciate the quick package. A few items our security/compliance team will need before we proceed with any production routing for EU accounts:

2) SOC 2 Type II report (redacted is fine) and a summary of any outstanding remediation items.

4) Confirmation that cache content for EU customers will not be egressed outside EU regions, or if it is, under what conditions and with what safeguards.
5) Data flow diagram that identifies where logs are ingested, pseudonymized, and stored.

If you can send the SOC2 and the expanded roster with a couple of rows expanded for LogSight (EU tenancy option vs US fallback), that would help us accelerate.

Ccd Kimberly from our compliance team to track this. Kimberly  can you confirm the minimal package well accept for a first-pass approval?

Tessa / Kimberly,

Thanks for the ping. Quick review notes from our side after scanning the spreadsheet and dataflow:

- SOC2 Type II: requested; if they can provide the 2027 report (even redacted), that will cover the baseline for operational controls.
- LogSight (US HQ): conditional accept if they can demonstrate EU tenancy for EU customers and an enforceable contractual requirement that logs for EU customers remain in the EU unless explicit written request. If there is any fallback to US processing, we need details and a mitigation plan (anonymization/pseudonymization before egress).
- Key management: if CacheVelocity cannot support customer-managed KMS, wed want an HSM attestation and the location of KMS/HSM (EU-only acceptable).
- CDN cache: require clause in DPA addendum that cache content for EU customers will be pinned to EU nodes except for temporary failover (define allowed failover conditions).
- Logging retention: ask for retention windows by processor and a deletion policy tied to Redwood customer requests.

Attachments Im including: SOC2 checklist (what we check), a short DPA clause draft wed like to include, and a sample evidence request. For initial gating, SOC2 + expanded roster + explicit statement on EU tenancy for LogSight + KMS location should be sufficient.

If CacheVelocity can provide those, Legal will draft a DPA addendum (short) and we can move to a pilot. If they cannot provide EU tenancy for logs, we may still allow metadata-level metrics but not persistent logs.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

Hi Tessa / Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks for the detailed notes. Attached are the items you requested: SOC2 (redacted), an expanded subprocessor roster (row for LogSight expanded with EU tenancy flags), and an updated dataflow PDF that highlights where pseudonymization occurs.

Key clarifications:
- LogSight: EU tenancy available and we will contractually require EU-only processing for Redwoods EU customers. If an exceptional failover to the US is needed (disaster recovery), it requires written approval and will be pseudonymized prior to transfer.
- KMS: we operate HSM-backed keys in eu-central-1; we do not currently support customer-managed keys but keys for Redwood workloads are stored and managed in EU HSM clusters.
- Retention: default logs retention is 30 days for operational logs, 90 days for aggregate metrics; deletion-by-request SLA: 7 business days.

Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_2027.pdf, CacheVelocity_subprocessors_2028-09.xlsx (updated), CacheVelocity_svc_dataflow_v1.pdf (annotated)

Let us know if that covers what you need and well accept whatever DPA addendum language you propose.
